newsitem.title: LIBERIA: U.S. donates ballot boxes for Liberian poll.
newsitem.headline: U.S. donates ballot boxes for Liberian poll.

text.p: The United States donated 2,000 transparent ballot boxes on Friday for Liberia's July 19 elections wrapping up a transition from years of civil war.

U.S. Ambassdor William Milam handed the boxes and ballot papers to Independent Elections Commission chairman Henry Andrews. He said the gift showed Washington's interest in seeing free, fair and democratic elections in the West African nation.
Liberia was founded by freed American slaves in 1847 and the United States remains the most influential Western power there.
Andrews said the ballot papers were printed in the Ghanaian capital Accra "under strict security".
The boxes and other ballot supplies were flown in from Denmark under the sponsorhip of U.S.-based International Foundation for Electoral Systems.
The elections commission this week overruled calls for a postponement by 12 of 13 parties contesting the presidential and general elections on grounds of alleged irregularities in voter registration.
Andrews said such a delay would be a recipe for further trouble in the country that has been torn by civil war and being without efective government for seven years.

Regional power Nigeria which leads a West African force policing Liberia since 1990 also ruled out a delay. Western donors led by the United States cautioned aid to Liberia could dry up if the faltering poll programme went off course again.
